topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under the Michigan Occupational Code, which state entity is created to oversee real estate brokers and salespersons?
choice_a: A standalone Michigan Real Estate Commission independent of LARA
choice_b: The State Board of Real Estate Appraisers, which also regulates brokers
choice_c: The Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons, created within the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA)
choice_d: The Bureau of Professional Licensing acting alone with no separate board
explanation: MCL 339.2502 creates 'the board of real estate brokers and salespersons,' and MCL 339.307(1) provides that every board created by the Occupational Code, including this one, is created within the department (LARA). Michigan has no separate independent 'Real Estate Commission'; brokers/salespersons and appraisers are overseen by different statutory boards.
source_note: MCL 339.2502; MCL 339.307(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: How is the 9-voting-member Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons composed under MCL 339.301?
choice_a: 5 members who hold a real estate license and 4 members who represent the general public
choice_b: 7 members who hold a real estate license and 2 members who represent the general public
choice_c: 9 members who must all hold an active real estate broker license
choice_d: 6 members who hold a real estate license and 3 members who represent the general public
explanation: MCL 339.301 provides that, unless an article of the code specifies otherwise, each occupational board consists of 9 voting members: 6 who are licensed or registered in the regulated occupation and 3 who represent the general public. Members must also be at least 18 years old and Michigan residents.
source_note: MCL 339.301 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: What role does the LARA director play on the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons?
choice_a: An ex officio member without a vote, who is not counted toward a quorum
choice_b: A full voting 10th member added to the 9 statutory members
choice_c: The chairperson, who casts the deciding vote in the event of a tie
choice_d: The director has no role on or connection to the board
explanation: MCL 339.301 makes the director an ex officio member of every occupational board without a vote, and specifies that the director is not counted as a member for purposes of determining a quorum.
source_note: MCL 339.301 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: For the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons to conduct official business, what constitutes a quorum, and can a member vote by proxy?
choice_a: Any 3 members constitute a quorum, and proxy voting is permitted with written authorization
choice_b: A majority of the members appointed and serving constitutes a quorum, and proxy voting is prohibited
choice_c: All 9 members must be present, and proxy voting is prohibited
choice_d: A majority constitutes a quorum, and a member may vote by proxy for a single meeting only
explanation: MCL 339.305 states that a majority of the members appointed and serving constitute a quorum for board business and expressly prohibits voting by proxy. Board meetings must also comply with Michigan's Open Meetings Act (1976 PA 267, MCL 15.261-15.275).
source_note: MCL 339.305 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under MCL 339.307, what are the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons' duties within the Department?
choice_a: To independently investigate and prosecute all license violations without any department involvement
choice_b: To issue and revoke licenses directly, bypassing the department entirely
choice_c: To interpret licensure and registration requirements, assist the department with investigations, optionally attend informal conferences, and otherwise assist in implementing the Occupational Code
choice_d: Solely to write and administer the licensing examination
explanation: MCL 339.307 creates each board within the department and charges it with interpreting licensure/registration requirements, assisting the department in investigations conducted under Article 5, optionally attending informal conferences under section 508, and generally assisting the department in implementing the act. The board is not an independent investigative or prosecutorial body -- it operates within, and in aid of, the department.
source_note: MCL 339.307 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: How is the director who heads the Department (LARA) for purposes of the Occupational Code appointed, and how long does the director serve?
choice_a: Elected by licensees of the regulated occupations to a fixed 4-year term
choice_b: Appointed by the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons for a renewable 6-year term
choice_c: Appointed by the senate majority leader without gubernatorial involvement
choice_d: Appointed by the governor with the advice and consent of the senate, and holds office at the pleasure of the governor
explanation: MCL 339.201 provides that the department consists of a director as executive head, appointed by the governor subject to the advice and consent of the senate, who holds office at the pleasure of the governor -- there is no fixed term of years.
source_note: MCL 339.201 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: MCL 339.201 requires the department to designate only investigators who meet the licensure qualifications of the profession being investigated -- for which occupations does this specific requirement apply?
choice_a: Only occupations regulated under Articles 7, 20, or 22 -- the sentence does not name real estate brokers and salespersons (Article 25) specifically
choice_b: Every occupation regulated anywhere in the Occupational Code, including real estate
choice_c: Only real estate brokers and salespersons under Article 25
choice_d: Only attorneys retained by the department of attorney general
explanation: MCL 339.201 limits this specific qualified-investigator requirement to occupations regulated under Articles 7, 20, and 22; Article 25 (real estate brokers and salespersons) is not among the articles named in that sentence. The general complaint-and-investigation machinery of Article 5 (MCL 339.501 et seq.) still applies broadly to real estate complaints regardless.
source_note: MCL 339.201 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under MCL 339.502, what must the department do upon receiving a complaint against a real estate licensee?
choice_a: Wait 30 days before opening any file, then decide whether to investigate
choice_b: Immediately begin investigating the allegations, open a correspondence file, and provide written notice to the complainant within 15 days
choice_c: Refer the complaint directly to a circuit court for review before taking any department action
choice_d: Immediately suspend the licensee's license pending a hearing
explanation: MCL 339.502 requires the department to immediately begin its investigation of a complaint's allegations and open a correspondence file, and to give the complainant written notice of the complaint within 15 days. If the department itself initiates the complaint, the director designates one or more employees to act as the complaining party.
source_note: MCL 339.502 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: How quickly must the department's investigative unit report to the director on the status of an investigation into a real estate complaint, and can that period be extended?
choice_a: Within 10 days, with no extensions permitted under any circumstance
choice_b: Within 90 days, with a single automatic 30-day extension
choice_c: Within 30 days after the department receives the complaint, with extensions available for good cause
choice_d: There is no statutory reporting deadline for investigations
explanation: MCL 339.504(1) requires the investigative unit to report to the director on the status of an investigation within 30 days of the department's receipt of the complaint. The director may grant extensions of that period for good cause, and the total number of extensions is tracked in the department's annual report under section 212.
source_note: MCL 339.504(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: If the department's investigation of a real estate complaint reveals a violation, which actions does MCL 339.504(3) authorize as an appropriate response?
choice_a: Only referral to the state police for criminal prosecution
choice_b: Only immediate, non-appealable revocation of the license
choice_c: Only a private letter of reprimand, with no further process available
choice_d: A formal complaint, a cease and desist order, a notice of summary suspension, or a citation
explanation: MCL 339.504(3) provides that once a violation is found, the department or the department of attorney general may prepare a formal complaint, a cease and desist order, a notice of summary suspension, or a citation as the appropriate action against the respondent.
source_note: MCL 339.504(3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: On what basis may the department issue an order summarily suspending a real estate license under MCL 339.505 before any hearing is held?
choice_a: An affidavit from a person familiar with the facts (or, if appropriate, on information and belief) showing an imminent threat to the public health, safety, and welfare
choice_b: A simple majority vote of the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons at a regular meeting
choice_c: Any single unverified complaint, regardless of its content
choice_d: A conviction of any misdemeanor unrelated to real estate practice
explanation: MCL 339.505(1) allows the department, after conducting an investigation, to summarily suspend a license based on an affidavit establishing that an imminent threat to the public health, safety, and welfare exists.
source_note: MCL 339.505(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: After a real estate licensee's license is summarily suspended, what happens if the licensee petitions the department to dissolve the suspension order?
choice_a: The suspension automatically dissolves after 10 days regardless of any hearing
choice_b: The department must immediately schedule a hearing, and an administrative law hearings examiner must grant the requested relief unless sufficient evidence shows an imminent threat still requires the suspension to continue
choice_c: The licensee must wait for the full contested case hearing on the merits before any relief is available
choice_d: Only the governor may dissolve a summary suspension order
explanation: MCL 339.505(2)-(3) requires the department to immediately schedule a hearing on a petition to dissolve a summary suspension, and directs the administrative law hearings examiner to grant relief dissolving the order unless sufficient evidence of a continuing imminent threat to public health, safety, and welfare is presented. The record from that hearing becomes part of the record in any later contested case hearing.
source_note: MCL 339.505(2), (3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: When the department serves a formal complaint on a real estate licensee under MCL 339.508, what options does the licensee have, and by when must a choice be made?
choice_a: The licensee has 60 days to respond in writing or the complaint is automatically dismissed
choice_b: The licensee's only option is to proceed to a contested case hearing; no settlement or compliance option exists
choice_c: Within 15 days, the licensee may choose to negotiate a settlement, demonstrate compliance before a contested hearing, or proceed directly to a contested case hearing -- failing to choose results in a contested case hearing
choice_d: The licensee must retain the department's own attorney to respond within 5 days
explanation: MCL 339.508(1)-(2) gives the respondent three options after being served a formal complaint -- negotiate a settlement, demonstrate compliance under Administrative Procedures Act section 92, or proceed to a contested case hearing under APA section 71 -- to be selected within 15 days of receiving notice; failing to select an option results in the department proceeding to a contested case hearing.
source_note: MCL 339.508(1), (2) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: What can an informal conference under MCL 339.508 result in, and can the Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons reject a proposed settlement reached there?
choice_a: It can only result in complete dismissal of the complaint, and the board has no authority to review it
choice_b: It automatically becomes final and binding the moment the licensee signs it, with no board review possible
choice_c: It can only impose a fine; suspension or revocation is never available through an informal conference
choice_d: It can result in a settlement, consent order, waiver, or default, with possible outcomes including revocation, suspension, limitation, censure, probation, or restitution -- and yes, the board may reject the settlement and require a contested case hearing instead
explanation: MCL 339.508(3) describes the range of informal-conference resolutions (settlement, consent order, waiver, default) and the resulting penalty options, and expressly allows the board to reject a proposed settlement and require a contested case hearing.
source_note: MCL 339.508(3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: How does the department obtain a subpoena to compel a witness to testify or produce documents in a real estate disciplinary proceeding?
choice_a: The department or the department of attorney general petitions a circuit court to issue the subpoena
choice_b: The Board of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons issues subpoenas directly, without any court involvement
choice_c: Only the administrative law hearings examiner may issue a subpoena, and only after a final order
choice_d: Subpoenas are unavailable in Occupational Code disciplinary proceedings
explanation: MCL 339.512 authorizes the department or the department of attorney general to petition a circuit court for a subpoena requiring a person to appear, testify, or produce documentary material for a proceeding conducted under section 511 or 508.
source_note: MCL 339.512 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Once a hearing report is issued in a real estate disciplinary case, how much time does MCL 339.514 give the board to determine the penalty it assesses under its MCL 339.309 authority?
choice_a: 10 business days, with no possibility of extension
choice_b: 60 days after receiving the administrative law examiner's hearing report (or 60 days after receiving a transcript, if one is ordered)
choice_c: 1 year, matching the standard limitations period for civil actions
choice_d: There is no deadline; the board may take as long as it wishes
explanation: MCL 339.514(1) gives the board 60 days after receiving the administrative law examiner's report to determine the penalty, or 60 days after receiving a transcript if one was ordered. MCL 339.309 confirms that the board assesses this penalty upon completion of a hearing conducted under section 511. If the board misses the deadline, the director may determine the penalty and issue a final order for occupations regulated under Articles 8 through 25.
source_note: MCL 339.514(1); MCL 339.309 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: MCL 339.514(3) bars which board member from participating in the final penalty determination on a real estate disciplinary complaint?
choice_a: Any board member who is also a licensed real estate broker
choice_b: Any board member who has served on the board for less than one year
choice_c: A board member who participated in investigating the complaint or attended an informal conference on that same complaint
choice_d: No board member is ever barred from participating
explanation: MCL 339.514(3) disqualifies a board member who participated in investigating the complaint, or who attended an informal conference on it, from taking part in the board's final determination of that same complaint, preserving the impartiality of the decision.
source_note: MCL 339.514(3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: What limitation does MCL 339.2515(2) place on the department when pursuing disciplinary charges against a real estate licensee?
choice_a: The department may assume any fact alleged in the complaint is true unless the licensee disproves it
choice_b: The licensee bears the burden of proving their own innocence once a complaint is filed
choice_c: No burden-of-proof standard applies in Occupational Code disciplinary hearings
choice_d: The department may not assume facts not in evidence or compel a party to prove innocence before charges are proven, and the department bears the burden of proof on all charges at all times
explanation: MCL 339.2515(2) expressly states that Article 25 does not authorize the department to assume facts not in evidence or compel a party to prove innocence of charges before the charges have been proven, and that the department bears the burden of proof on all charges at all times. Subsection (3) further preserves a party's right to pursue direct legal or equitable remedies in court.
source_note: MCL 339.2515(2), (3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under the Article 25 exemptions in MCL 339.2503(1), which of the following persons is generally exempt from real estate broker/salesperson licensure?
choice_a: An owner or lessor (or their attorney-in-fact acting under a duly executed and recorded power of attorney, or a court-appointed person) dealing with property they own, unless doing so as a principal vocation and not through a licensed broker
choice_b: Any person who sells more than 3 properties per year for other owners, regardless of licensure
choice_c: A property management company managing rental units it does not own
choice_d: A real estate salesperson working without an assigned supervising broker
explanation: MCL 339.2503(1) exempts an owner or lessor -- and an attorney-in-fact acting under a duly executed and recorded power of attorney, or a person appointed by a court -- performing broker/salesperson-type acts with reference to property they own, unless performed as a principal vocation and not through a licensed real estate broker. The same subsection separately exempts an owner who, as owner, sells a never-before-occupied detached single-family, duplex, triplex, or quadruplex dwelling the owner built while licensed under Article 24.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(1) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Which of the following is exempt from Article 25 licensure under MCL 339.2503(2)?
choice_a: A title insurance agent closing residential transactions
choice_b: An attorney-at-law rendering services as an attorney, or a receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, administrator, or executor selling real estate under court order
choice_c: A licensed appraiser performing a fee appraisal for a lender
choice_d: A mortgage loan officer originating a purchase-money loan
explanation: MCL 339.2503(2) exempts an attorney-at-law who is rendering services as an attorney-at-law, and a receiver, trustee in bankruptcy, administrator, executor, or person selling real estate under order of a court, from Article 25 licensure -- with a further carve-out for a deed-of-trust trustee who makes repeated or successive sales of real estate not through a licensed broker.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(2) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: MCL 339.2503(3) exempts which category of person from Article 25 real estate licensure?
choice_a: Any bank employee, regardless of what real estate activities they perform
choice_b: A person who has ever held a real estate license in another state
choice_c: A person regulated under the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act who does not perform any other act requiring a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson license
choice_d: A licensed home inspector performing inspections incidental to a sale
explanation: MCL 339.2503(3) exempts a person who is regulated under the Mortgage Brokers, Lenders, and Servicers Licensing Act, 1987 PA 173 (MCL 445.1651-445.1684), from Article 25 licensure, provided that person does not also perform any other act that would otherwise require a real estate broker, associate broker, or salesperson license.
source_note: MCL 339.2503(3) (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under MCL 339.602, which of the following administrative penalties may be assessed against a real estate licensee found to have violated the Occupational Code?
choice_a: Only a flat $500 fine per violation, with no other remedy available
choice_b: Automatic permanent revocation, with no lesser penalty option
choice_c: Only criminal misdemeanor prosecution; no administrative fine is authorized
choice_d: Limitation, suspension, denial, or revocation of the license; an administrative fine of not more than $10,000; censure; probation; or restitution
explanation: MCL 339.602 lists the administrative penalties available for a violation of the Occupational Code (or a rule or order issued under it), including placement of a limitation on, suspension of, denial of, or revocation of a license; an administrative fine of not more than $10,000; censure; probation; and restitution based on proofs submitted to and findings made by the hearing examiner.
source_note: MCL 339.602 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: MCL 339.604 lists grounds for discipline that apply broadly across occupations regulated by the code. Which of the following is one of those grounds?
choice_a: Practicing fraud or deceit in obtaining a license, or failing to comply with a subpoena issued under the act
choice_b: Advertising a licensee's own name in a local newspaper
choice_c: Taking continuing education courses beyond the minimum required hours
choice_d: Holding more than one professional license simultaneously
explanation: MCL 339.604 lists prohibited conduct subject to the section 602 penalties, including practicing fraud or deceit in obtaining or practicing a licensed occupation, gross negligence, false advertising, incompetence, lack of good moral character, failing to comply with a subpoena issued under the act, failing to comply with a final board order, and aiding or abetting unlicensed practice.
source_note: MCL 339.604 (confirmed via live fetch of legislature.mi.gov 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: Under Michigan Administrative Code R 339.1708, for how long after a real estate license lapses, is surrendered, or is revoked does the former licensee remain subject to discipline for code violations committed while licensed?
choice_a: Discipline is no longer possible once the license lapses, regardless of when the violation occurred
choice_b: Until the later of 7 years after the change in status or full compliance with all final orders
choice_c: A flat 1-year period following the change in license status, with no compliance-based extension
choice_d: Discipline can only be pursued while the license remains active
explanation: R 339.1708(3) provides that a person who loses licensure or registration status remains subject to disciplinary action for violations of the code, promulgated rules, or a final order until the later of 7 years after the change in status, or full compliance with all final orders. R 339.1708(1) further clarifies that discipline applies regardless of whether the person later becomes licensed again, or whether the department knew of the violation when a license was granted.
source_note: Mich Admin Code R 339.1708 (confirmed via live fetch of the department's Administrative Rules System, ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us, 2026-08-31)

topic: Duties and Powers of the Department and State Board
question: How may the department effect valid service of a formal complaint, suspension order, or final order on a real estate licensee under Michigan Administrative Code R 339.1710?
choice_a: Only by certified mail, with service deemed received the same day it is postmarked
choice_b: Only by personal service; mail service of any kind is invalid
choice_c: By personal service, first-class U.S. mail, or certified mail return receipt requested, sent to the most current address of record on file with the department -- mailed service is deemed received 3 business days after mailing unless the certified mail receipt shows otherwise
choice_d: By publication in a newspaper of general circulation, with no direct notice to the licensee required
explanation: R 339.1710 permits service by personal service, first-class mail, or certified mail return receipt requested to the licensee's most current address of record; deems mailed service received 3 business days after the date of mailing (absent contrary evidence from the returned certified mail receipt); and provides that a respondent's refusal to accept delivery does not invalidate service.
source_note: Mich Admin Code R 339.1710 (confirmed via live fetch of the department's Administrative Rules System, ars.apps.lara.state.mi.us, 2026-08-31)
